pr_body:

issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

**Note**: Please read [this guide](https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports) detailing how to provide the necessary information for us to reproduce your bug.

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
# Your code here
import pandas
import numpy as np
df = pandas.DataFrame(np.arange(64))
length = len(df.index)
df.index = [(i - length / 2) % length for i in range(length)]
df.sort_index(axis=0, ascending=None, na_position="first")
ValueError: the 'axis' parameter is not supported in the pandas implementation of argsort()
```

#### Problem description

There was no such issue in pandas version 1.1.5

comments: The same is true for Series.sort_index(...).

`ascending` is an argument which accepts boolean or list of booleans. I do not believe it should be considered a bug or a regression if the execution has changed from one version to another with an erroneous input argument.

I would not know what output to expect with `ascending=None`?
we should be validating the ascending arg type as boolean - it's possible we r not

> I would not know what output to expect with `ascending=None`?

As I see, `ascending=None` and `ascending=False` behaviors were identical in 1.1.5 version. So, I think it would be good to add a check for `ascending`.

> There was no such issue in pandas version 1.1.5

first bad commit: [aa43f17357fec66e7cb2323dd3ba327bc16dd6c5] REF: nargsort incorrectly calling _values_for_argsort (#37266)

> As I see, `ascending=None` and `ascending=False` behaviors were identical in 1.1.5 version. So, I think it would be good to add a check for `ascending`.

@ivanovmg  an alternative could be to restore the old behaviour for 1.2.x and repurpose #39451 for 1.3 and then  can advertise the 'breaking change', which is permissible since the usage is incorrect.
no i think we should just fix this - the. new is wrong

review_comments: can you add the issue number as a comment
also could change docstring `bool or list of bools` -> `bool or list-like of bools`
Union[bool, Sequence[bool]]. int is no-where in this. same for all the others.
and docstring L3062 `ascending : bool, default True` should be updated to match

This is required for ``validate_ascending`` as int is actually considered as a valid boolean there.
Previously I had this check in ``validate_ascending`` itself, but I was requested to use ``validate_boolean``, so I extended it in such a way.

It may be necessary to maybe restrict ``ascending`` to use of booleans only (no integers), but this is a breaking change and should probably be discussed first.
if `validate_bool_kwarg` allowed ints through before, wouldn't `int_allowed` need to default to True for backwards compatibility?

I checked ``is_bool``, and by default it considers ``int`` as a non-boolean.

```
In [1]: from pandas.core.dtypes.common import is_bool

In [2]: is_bool(1)
Out[2]: False
```
you don't need allow of this, just call `validate_bool_kwarg`

``validate_bool_kwargs`` accepts ``None`` as a valid value.
Do we consider ``ascending=None`` as valid?
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/39434#issuecomment-768407714

in this case no
so i can enhance the checker with an arg to only allow an actual bool
pls use `validate_bool_kwarg` instead of adding *anything* here. you can add a kwargs to that function itself to make things strict

``ascending`` here may be a single value or a sequence of items.
I am afraid that I still need to add validation of either a scalar value or each of the items in the sequence.
in the def we have `ascending: bool_t = True`, so should probably update that too as part of this PR.

I did that in order to match the expected type for ``ascending`` in ``nargsort`` function.
It must be ``bool`` as per the function signature.
However, at this particular point ``ascending`` can be an integer as well (previously it was allowed).
